dfd_element: Mobile Client -> API Gateway: ID image + selfie
threat_description: A stable account or device context can allow repeated identity-verification attempts to be linked across sessions, enabling behavioral profiling beyond the immediate onboarding purpose.
attacker_capability: Observer or service operator able to correlate persistent identifiers, session metadata, device attributes, or repeated verification events.
affected_data: Account identifier; device metadata; session identifiers; verification timestamps

dfd_element: IDVerify Service -> Third-Party OCR / Face-Match API
threat_description: The third-party provider may correlate selfie and identity-document submissions from the same person across repeated checks or across multiple customers if persistent identifiers or biometric templates are retained.
attacker_capability: Third-party processor with access to request metadata, biometric inputs, retained templates, or customer identifiers.
affected_data: Selfie; face template; ID image; extracted identity attributes; request metadata

threat_description: Centralized storage of identity attributes, verification outcomes, account references, and timestamps can enable linkage of previously separate personal-data sets into a richer individual profile.
attacker_capability: Database administrator, compromised application account, insider, or attacker with query access.
affected_data: Name; document number; DOB; nationality; verification history; account reference

dfd_element: IDVerify Service -> Third-Party OCR / Face-Match API
threat_description: A selfie or identity-document image can directly reveal or permit inference of the natural person's identity even if an application-level user identifier is pseudonymous.
attacker_capability: Third-party provider, attacker intercepting plaintext inside the recipient environment, or compromised processor account.
affected_data: Face image; passport or national ID image; name; document number

threat_description: Extracted PII stored together with verification status can allow a pseudonymous application record to be resolved to a named individual.
attacker_capability: Database reader able to access identity attributes and application identifiers.
affected_data: Full name; Emirates ID/passport number; date of birth; user/account identifier

threat_description: Detailed immutable audit records tying a specific officer or user to an identity-verification action may create excessive proof of behavior beyond what is necessary for accountability, reducing the individual's ability to plausibly deny actions.
attacker_capability: Compliance administrator, insider, investigator, or party with access to detailed logs.
affected_data: Officer identity; user reference; timestamp; verification action; decision

dfd_element: Admin Dashboard -> IDVerify Service: review decision
threat_description: Persistently binding a compliance officer identity to every review decision can create an unnecessary long-term behavioral record if less identifying accountability evidence would suffice.
attacker_capability: Administrator or auditor with dashboard and audit-log access.
affected_data: Officer identifier; review decision; case identifier; timestamp

threat_description: Differences in response codes, response size, or timing may reveal whether an identity or account already exists or whether a document has previously been submitted.
attacker_capability: Remote unauthenticated or low-privilege attacker capable of sending repeated API requests and measuring responses.
affected_data: Account existence; onboarding status; document registration status

dfd_element: API Gateway -> Mobile Client: verification result
threat_description: Distinct rejected, approved, and manual-review responses may expose sensitive facts about whether a user triggered fraud, biometric, or document-validation rules.
attacker_capability: Remote observer, malicious client, or user able to compare detailed response behavior.
affected_data: Verification outcome; manual-review status; fraud indicators

dfd_element: Mobile Client -> API Gateway: ID image + selfie
threat_description: The client transmits complete identity-document and facial images even when downstream processing may require only a subset of attributes, creating excessive collection and exposure.
attacker_capability: Compromised client, network-adjacent attacker under failed transport protection, backend insider, or service compromise.
affected_data: Full ID image; selfie; document metadata; facial characteristics

dfd_element: IDVerify Service -> Third-Party OCR / Face-Match API
threat_description: Full-resolution identity documents and selfies may be disclosed to the external ML provider even where on-device preprocessing or field minimization could reduce the information shared.
attacker_capability: Third-party provider, processor insider, compromised third-party tenant, or external attacker.
affected_data: ID image; face image; biometric-derived information; document number; DOB; nationality

threat_description: The datastore retains extracted PII and verification status in a form accessible to the application even after the onboarding decision no longer requires all raw attributes.
attacker_capability: Database administrator, compromised service identity, application vulnerability, or insider.
affected_data: Extracted PII; document identifiers; verification status; biometric-related results

threat_description: Audit events may copy personal identifiers or biometric-processing metadata into a secondary store, creating an unnecessary duplicate dataset with a longer retention period.
attacker_capability: Logging administrator, SIEM user, attacker with log-store access, or downstream analytics consumer.
affected_data: User identifier; document reference; IP address; verification event; match score; timestamps

dfd_element: Mobile Client -> IDVerify Service -> Third-Party OCR / Face-Match API
threat_description: The individual may not understand that their selfie and identity document leave the fintech trust boundary and are processed by a third-party ML provider.
attacker_capability: System operator or processor benefiting from insufficient transparency; threat arises from design rather than technical compromise.
affected_data: Selfie; ID image; biometric processing; third-party recipient identity

threat_description: A user may not know that an automated verification outcome triggered human review or may lack a practical mechanism to contest an incorrect biometric or OCR result.
attacker_capability: System operator with insufficient notice, appeal, or correction workflow.
affected_data: Verification result; match score; extracted identity attributes; reviewer decision

threat_description: The external processor may retain submitted identity images, biometric-derived data, or telemetry beyond the documented purpose or retention period, conflicting with minimization and storage-limitation requirements.
attacker_capability: Third-party processor with technical ability to retain inputs, outputs, logs, or derived models.
affected_data: Selfie; ID image; face template; extracted PII; service telemetry

dfd_element: IDVerify Service / PostgreSQL / Audit Logging Service
threat_description: The architecture may lack enforceable retention, deletion, purpose-limitation, access-review, and privacy-default controls across primary data and secondary audit stores.
attacker_capability: System owner, administrator, or engineering process lacking automated governance controls.
affected_data: All identity-verification personal data and audit records
